NSCI 140.title: The Learning Brain
NSCI 140.description: Applications and implications of neuroscience for society and the individual, with a focus on neuroplasticity and neuroeducation. Not for credit for students who have credit for, or are currently taking, NSCI_V 200.

NSCI 200.title: Fundamentals of Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience
NSCI 200.description: Introduction to the field of neuroscience in general, and the fields of cellular and molecular neuroscience in particular, with emphasis on neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, and neuropharmacology.

children.raw: 2nd-year class standing or higher in the Neuroscience specialization
8 credits of CHEM_V 1st and 6 credits of BIOL_V 1st

NSCI 200.prerequisiteText: One of: a) 2nd-year class standing or higher in the Neuroscience specialization, or b) 8 credits of CHEM_V 1st and 6 credits of BIOL_V 1st

NSCI 201.title: Fundamentals of Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience
NSCI 201.description: Emphasis on the relationship between behaviour or cognition and nervous system function.

NSCI 210.title: Research Design for the Neurosciences
NSCI 210.description: A focus on research design relevant to the neurosciences, with an emphasis on engagement with the scientific process, from question formulation to knowledge translation.
NSCI 210.prerequisiteText: NSCI_V 200 and one of STAT_V 200, STAT_V 201, BIOL_V 300, PSYC_V 218, PSYO_O 271, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 230

NSCI 300.title: Laboratory Techniques for the Neurosciences
NSCI 300.description: Laboratory techniques for investigating nervous system function, and for establishing relationships between nervous system function, behaviour, and cognition. Restricted to students in the Neuroscience specialization.

NSCI 301.title: Neuroscience, Ethics, and Society
NSCI 301.description: Ethical issues associated with neuroscience, and the impact of neuroscience on society.
NSCI 301.prerequisiteText: One of NSCI_V 201, PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 344, PSYC_V 370, BIOL_V 371

NSCI 302.title: Neurodiversity, Brain Injury, and Brain Illness
NSCI 302.description: Conceptual frameworks, defining features, and neurobiological mechanisms of the diverse, injured, or diseased brain.
NSCI 302.prerequisiteText: One of NSCI_V 201, PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 344, PSYC_V 371, BIOL_V 372

NSCI 303.title: Foundations of Computational Neuroscience
NSCI 303.description: Foundations of computational neuroscience: neural modelling, simple neural networks, models of Hebbian learning, models of learning, clustering and classification.
NSCI 303.prerequisiteText: One of NSCI_V 201, PSYC_V 371, BIOL_V 371 and one of DSCI_V 100, CPSC_V 103, CPSC_V 110 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184

NSCI 311.title: Advanced Neuroanatomy
NSCI 311.description: Detailed coverage of neuroanatomy, with applications

NSCI 398.title: Cooperative Work Placement I
NSCI 398.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in Summer Session after third year. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Neuroscience.

prerequisite.raw: Co-op workshops, and third-year standing in the neuroscience specialization

NSCI 398.prerequisiteText: Co-op workshops, and third-year standing in the neuroscience specialization

NSCI 399.title: Cooperative Work Placement II
NSCI 399.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in Term 1 of the 4th Year Winter Session. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Neuroscience.

NSCI 400.title: Neuroscience Capstone
NSCI 400.description: A capstone course to provide students with a rigorous neuroscience research experience under the supervision of one or more faculty members. Integrated support and feedback is provided by peers and faculty.

prerequisite.raw: Restricted to students in the neuroscience specialization

NSCI 400.prerequisiteText: Restricted to students in the neuroscience specialization

NSCI 401.title: Your Position in the Neurosciences
NSCI 401.description: Practices to promote equity, diversity, inclusion, and decolonization in the neurosciences, and exploration of one's positionality through historical and present-day neuroscience.
NSCI 401.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 372, NSCI_V 201, PSYC_V 301, PSYC_V 304, PSYC_V 371

NSCI 448.title: Directed Studies in Neuroscience
NSCI 448.description: Directed investigation of a neuroscience research question requiring a report of the findings. No more than six credits of NSCI_V 448 may be taken with the same supervisor.

prerequisite.raw: At least a 70% average in the preceding 30 credits, permission of the supervisor, and permission of the director of the neuroscience specialization

NSCI 448.prerequisiteText: At least a 70% average in the preceding 30 credits, permission of the supervisor, and permission of the director of the neuroscience specialization

NSCI 486.title: Advanced Topics in Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience
NSCI 486.description: Selected topics in Behavioural and Cognitive Neuroscience. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the program.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing in a Neuroscience specialization

NSCI 486.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing in a Neuroscience specialization

NSCI 487.title: Advanced Topics in Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience
NSCI 487.description: Selected topics in Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the program.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing in a Neuroscience specialization

NSCI 487.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing in a Neuroscience specialization

NSCI 488.title: Topics in Neuroscience
NSCI 488.description: Selected topics in a specific area within Neuroscience. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the department.

prerequisite.raw: Third year standing in a Neuroscience specialization, and permission of an Advisor for the Undergraduate Program in Neuroscience

NSCI 488.prerequisiteText: Third year standing in a Neuroscience specialization, and permission of an Advisor for the Undergraduate Program in Neuroscience

NSCI 498.title: Cooperative Work Placement III
NSCI 498.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in Term 2 of the 4th Year Winter Session. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Neuroscience.

NSCI 499.title: Cooperative Work Placement IV
NSCI 499.description: Approved and supervised relevant work experience in an industrial, academic, or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks, full-time. Normally taken in the Summer Session after 4th year. Work term report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-op Program in Neuroscience.
